# Zenoh Profile 0 conformance corpus, read by the host tests in tests.rs.
#
# One vector per line; blank lines and '#' lines are comments. Fields are
# space-separated; an empty hex string is written '-'.
#
#   batch  <name> ok <hex> <summary>        a batch body (no stream length prefix) and its decoded summary
#   batch  <name> refused <class> <hex>     a batch body the profile must refuse
#   stream <name> ok <chunks> <batches> <pending>
#                                           chunks (comma-separated hex, '-' = empty chunk) fed to the
#                                           stream reassembler; the batches it yields (comma-separated
#                                           hex, '-' = none) and the bytes it still buffers
#   stream <name> refused <class> <chunks>
#
# Summary grammar: one string, no spaces; ';' separates fields, '|' separates
# network messages. The 'ok' summaries are written from the values given to the
# upstream encoder.
#
# Provenance. Every 'batch ... ok' vector was produced by the upstream
# eclipse-zenoh 1.0.0 encoder (zenoh-codec =1.0.0, zenoh-protocol =1.0.0,
# zenoh-buffers =1.0.0, wire version 0x09) and decoded back by it, so those
# bytes are independent of this codec. Every 'refused' and 'stream' vector is
# derived by hand from the profile's rules; nothing upstream checks them. The
# one exception is push_put_no_attachment_upstream_valid: upstream 1.0.0 encodes
# and accepts it, and Profile 0 refuses it because every sample carries the
# attachment whose sequence number is how a subscriber detects a replay.
#
# Wire facts taken from the 1.0.0 codec, not from the prose specification: the
# U_SUBSCRIBER WireExpr extension (id 0x0f, ZBuf, mandatory) carries
# <flags:u8><scope:z16> and then the raw suffix bytes to the end of the ZBuf,
# with no <u8;z16> length prefix of its own.
#
# The bounds are the frozen demo contract's (contracts/rpi5-ros2-demo/v2):
# 512-byte batch, 129-byte key expression, 33-byte attachment, 12-byte payload.
# The 64-byte cookie bound is contracts/zenoh-profile/v1's own choice.
